You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: When the target is itself a shadow host, its own shadow content is hidden.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Target H is a shadow host and `t` is also a target inside H's shadow root `S`: the sibling `s` of `t` in `S` is not hidden. Probe `expect(hidden(s)).toBe(true)` received `false`. Cause: `acceptNode` returns FILTER_REJECT for the visible host H before the shadow-walk branch runs, so `walk(S)` never happens. Expected per criterion 1.
- [blocking] `root` option inside a shadow root: `ariaHideOutside([t], container)` with `container` in shadow root S0, then `S0.append(outside)` makes `outside` aria-hidden. The light-DOM analogue (container in body, `body.append(outside)`) stays visible. The new observer on S0 ignores `root` and hides nodes outside it. No in-repo caller passes `root`, so impact is external callers only.
- [minor] Nested call: host H hidden by call 1 stays aria-hidden when call 2 targets content inside H's shadow root. Reproduced, but the light-DOM analogue behaves identically, so this is pre-existing semantics, not a regression.
- [minor] Target moved into an already-hidden empty container (`ext.append(h)` after `ext` was hidden on add) leaves the container aria-hidden. Reproduced in shadow; light-DOM analogue not run.
- [minor] Observed roots are computed once at call time. Moving the target's host into a different shadow root later is not observed. Not reproduced.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
Fix round 1. Repo /tmp/ff-eval-3f3sium4/workspace. Uncommitted change in packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts adds shadow DOM support (see `git diff`). Reproduced bug: with the flag on, when the `root` option is an element inside shadow root S0 (`ariaHideOutside([t], container)` where container is in S0 and t inside container), the observed-roots loop climbs past `root` and observes S0 (and further up), so `S0.append(outside)` makes `outside` aria-hidden — but nothing outside `root` may ever be hidden (light-DOM analogue: container in body, `body.append(outside)` stays visible). Fix: only observe shadow roots that are inside `root` (e.g. add a shadow root to observedRoots only while `nodeContains(root, shadowRoot.host)`; stop climbing otherwise). Keep the change minimal; flag-off path unchanged. Add a regression test to the existing shadow DOM describe in packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.test.js (root container inside a shadow root; appending a sibling of the container into that shadow root does not get aria-hidden; appending inside the container outside the target does get hidden).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Flag on, target T inside shadow root S (host H in document.body): T's siblings in S are hidden (aria-hidden="true", or inert with shouldUseInert); H and T are not hidden; H's siblings in body are hidden.
2. Nested: T in S2, whose host H2 is inside S1, whose host H1 is in body: siblings in S2, S1 and body are hidden; H1, H2, T are not.
3. A shadow host not on any target's path is hidden as a whole (aria-hidden on the host only; its shadow content is not individually marked).
4. Content added after the call anywhere in a target's shadow root, or any root enclosing it (S1, S2, body), is hidden. Content added inside a target, or inside an already-hidden node, is not marked. Added elements with data-live-announcer="true" / data-react-aria-top-layer="true" in those shadow roots stay visible; ones already present in those shadow roots at call time stay visible too.
5. Targets in different shadow roots (e.g. input in S_a, popover in S_b, both hosts in body): both targets and both hosts visible; siblings in S_a, S_b and body hidden; mutations in both S_a and S_b are observed.
6. The returned function removes every aria-hidden/inert it added, including inside shadow roots, and disconnects every observer: content added to any of those shadow roots afterwards is not hidden.
7. Nested calls: a second ariaHideOutside call disconnects the first's observers (including shadow ones); reverting the second re-observes the first's shadow roots (a later shadow mutation gets hidden by the first). Ref counting: an element hidden by two calls stays hidden until both revert; an element already aria-hidden before the call stays aria-hidden after revert.
8. A target slotted from light DOM into a host's shadow root stays visible (its host and the <slot> that renders it are not hidden).
9. A target that is itself a shadow host: its own shadow content is not hidden.
10. Flag off: behavior is unchanged; all existing tests in ariaHideOutside.test.js and the rest of packages/@react-aria/overlays/test, packages/@react-aria/combobox/test, packages/@react-aria/dnd/test pass unmodified.
11. Tests for 1–9 live in packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.test.js in a describe after the existing tests with enableShadowDOM() in beforeAll; `yarn eslint` on changed files and `yarn check-types` pass; overlays package.json declares @react-stately/flags.
